summary: Phase 2 frontend-only testing of Ghost Maze (Expo Web preview, 414x896). All 14 requested test cases PASSED. Main menu renders with both START GAME (testID 'play-btn') and CHARACTERS (testID 'characters-btn'). CHARACTERS navigates to /characters where the BACK button, stats panel (HIGH LEVEL/HIGH SCORE/TOTAL CATCHES/PERFECT CLEARS - all defaulting to 0/1), and 5 visible theme cards render correctly: theme-classic shows 'SELECTED' tag + '✓ Unlocked', and theme-neon, theme-spectre, theme-mono, theme-candy all show 'LOCKED' with their respective unlock hints ('Reach Level 3', 'Reach Level 5', 'Reach Level 7', '100 Total Catches'). BACK returns to main menu, START GAME navigates to /game. Game HUD shows LEVEL 1, SCORE, CATCHES 0/3, LIVES dots; pellets bar shows 124 total pellets. All 4 ghost D-pads and bottom controls (pause-btn/sound-btn/quit-btn) render. SOUND button toggles between '🔊 SOUND' and '🔇 MUTED' cleanly on each click. Game loop runs: score climbed 0→90→340→650 and pellets 124→115→90→64 over ~12s. Smooth animation verified: entity translateX offsets were fractional (e.g. 114.061, 240.245, 173.755) and changed gradually across 150ms snapshots, confirming Animated.timing interpolation works. Both new trap types appeared during play: red spike diamonds (#FF1144) and brown/orange barricades (#8B4513) observed in DOM scans. PAUSE button label correctly toggled PAUSE↔RESUME. QUIT triggered navigation back to main menu (visually confirmed via screenshot; selector timeout only because Expo Router on Web briefly keeps both /index and /game in the DOM tree during the route swap — non-issue). No red error screens or JS crashes during 30+ seconds of gameplay. No deprecated Expo packages detected (only expo-haptics in use, which is current).
critical_code_review_comments: Console emits 'Animated: useNativeDriver is not supported... Falling back to JS-based animation' on Web — expected for Expo Web (no RCTAnimation). Animations still work fine via JS driver. No code change needed; on native this will silently use the native driver.

Console emits 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' once. All four pointerEvents usages in our own code (game.tsx:269 and MazeRenderer.tsx:259/462/511/603) are already inside the style object, so the warning originates from a third-party dependency (likely react-native-safe-area-context or expo-router internals). Not actionable on our side.

Minor: characters.tsx loadProgress() runs once on mount; if user wins a level then navigates to /characters and back, unlocked themes reflect — but if /characters is opened in another tab/router stack frame that doesn't unmount, new unlocks won't appear until reload. Consider re-loading on focus via useFocusEffect for better UX (non-blocking).
seed_data_creation: None - client-side AsyncStorage progress data uses defaults (highestLevel=1, totalCatches=0, perfectClears=0, only 'classic' theme unlocked). Locked-state UI verified against fresh state.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All Phase 2 features verified on Web preview at 414x896: smooth tile-to-tile animation (fractional translateX confirmed), sound engine UI toggle (Web Audio API playback can't be heard headlessly but the button toggles state, calls setEnabled/startMusic/stopMusic without error), trap system (spike diamonds and brown/orange barricades both appeared organically in the maze during ~25s of gameplay), and the characters/progression screen with all locked-state UI. Sound playback itself isn't asserted because Web Audio requires a user-gesture-after-load and headless browsers commonly suspend ctx. Score/pellet counters run smoothly via requestAnimationFrame. After QUIT, expect Expo Router to briefly keep two 'main-menu' nodes in the DOM during the route swap — use page.locator(...).first() if asserting visibility post-QUIT.
